items.title: Humanity's Sixth Sense: Benchmarking Intuitive Visual Reasoning in Multimodal Models
items.content: Humans perceive far more in a scene than what is explicitly depicted: a single glance captures past causes and future trajectories; a quick peek determines if a vehicle can fit between two parked cars; a few seconds of video reveals who holds authority in a room; and a fleeting clip highlights subtle abstract patterns like unwritten rules or hidden labels. This capacity reflects a form of humanity's sixth sense: an intuitive reasoning mechanism that recovers implicit information beyond raw senso
items.author: HF Daily Papers
items.summary: An HF Daily Papers listing for an arXiv paper proposing a benchmark for intuitive visual reasoning in multimodal models. The paper argues humans recover implicit information beyond raw sensory input - past causes, future trajectories, spatial fit judgments, social authority cues, and abstract unwritten rules - from brief glances or clips, and formalizes this as a sixth sense to test in multimodal LLMs.
